title: Print Your Current Directory
prompt: You are inside a nested folder and want to print the full absolute path of your current working directory.
explanation: pwd outputs the full absolute path from the filesystem root (/) to your current directory.

title: Create 1000 Folders in One Command
prompt: Create 1000 folders named folder_1 through folder_1000 in a single command using brace expansion.
explanation: Brace expansion {1..1000} expands into 1000 arguments passed to mkdir in one shot.

title: Move Up to the Parent Directory
prompt: You are currently inside /Users/karansharma/practice. Move back up one level into /Users/karansharma.
hint: Use cd followed by the parent directory symbol.
explanation: In every folder, '..' refers to the parent directory one level up.

title: Append Text Without Overwriting
prompt: Append the text "Line 2" to the end of notes.txt without overwriting its existing content.
explanation: '>>' redirects echo output to the end of the file, preserving existing lines.

title: Copy an Entire Folder
prompt: Copy the folder 'projects' and everything inside it to a new folder named 'projects_backup'.
hint: Plain cp fails on directories with 'Is a directory'. Add the recursive flag.
simulatedOutput: (Copied projects/ and all contents to projects_backup/)
explanation: The -r (recursive) flag is required for cp to copy directories and their contents.

title: Make a Script Executable
prompt: You created hello.txt with shell instructions inside, but ./hello.txt fails with 'permission denied'. Grant execute permission to hello.txt.
simulatedOutput: (Execute bit set on hello.txt — ./hello.txt can now run)
explanation: New files default to 644 (rw-r--r--) without execute permission for security. chmod +x enables execution.

title: Restrict File to Owner Read/Write Only
prompt: Set numeric permissions on secret.txt so ONLY the owner can read and write (rw-------), with zero permissions for group or others.
hint: Read = 4, Write = 2, Execute = 1. Owner = 4+2, Group = 0, Others = 0.
explanation: 600 gives Owner 6 (r+w = 4+2) and 0 (no permissions) to Group and Others.

title: Force-Terminate a Runaway Process
prompt: You spotted a runaway Python process in htop with PID 2341. Force it to terminate immediately using SIGKILL (signal 9).
hint: Use kill with the -9 flag and the PID.
explanation: kill <PID> sends polite SIGTERM (15); kill -9 <PID> sends SIGKILL (9) to force immediate termination.

title: Case-Insensitive Search with Line Numbers
prompt: Search server.log for the word "error" (case-insensitive) and display matching line numbers.
hint: Combine grep's -i (ignore case) and -n (line numbers) flags.
explanation: grep -i ignores case and -n prefixes each matching line with its line number.

title: Compress a File While Keeping the Original
prompt: Compress notes.txt using gzip into notes.txt.gz, while keeping the original notes.txt intact.
explanation: By default gzip replaces the original file with the .gz archive; -k preserves the original.

title: Initialize a Local Git Repository
prompt: Initialize a brand new Git repository in your current project folder.
hint: This command creates the hidden .git memory folder.
explanation: git init initializes version tracking by creating the hidden .git folder.

title: Stage and Commit a File
prompt: Stage notes.txt into the Staging Area (step 1), OR commit staged changes with message "Add notes" (write the git commit command).
explanation: git commit -m "<msg>" permanently records the staged snapshot into repository history.

title: Link Local Repo to GitHub Remote
prompt: Link your local repository to the GitHub remote URL https://github.com/NST/test.git under the nickname 'origin'.
explanation: git remote add origin <URL> registers the remote repository address so you can push and pull.

title: First-Time Project Download from GitHub
prompt: A teammate pushed code to https://github.com/NST/test.git. Download the entire project and its full Git history to your computer for the first time.
hint: Use git clone for a first-time download (git pull is for updating an existing repo).
explanation: git clone downloads the full project and its complete commit history for the first time.
